title: G2L: Semantically Aligned and Uniform Video Grounding via Geodesic and Game Theory

problems.name: Multi-Moment, Compositional, and Complex Query Grounding
problems.evidence_sentence: Due to two annoying issues in video grounding: (1) the co-existence of some visual entities in both ground truth and other moments, i.e. semantic overlapping; (2) only a few moments in the video are annotated, i.e. sparse annotation dilemma, vanilla contrastive learning is unable to model the correlations between temporally distant moments and learned inconsistent video representations.

problems.name: Cross-Modal Semantic Alignment Gap
problems.evidence_sentence: We quantify the correlations among moments leveraging the geodesic distance that guides the model to learn the correct cross-modal representations.

methods.name: Contrastive or Cross-Modal Alignment

methods.name: Query-Conditioned Frame/Clip Selection
methods.evidence_sentence: Furthermore, from the novel perspective of game theory, we propose semantic Shapley interaction based on geodesic distance sampling to learn fine-grained semantic alignment in similar moments.

methods.name: Benchmark or Dataset Construction
methods.evidence_sentence: Such severe data imbalance leads to signiﬁcant learning bias for vanilla contrastive learning, i.e., unannotated moments are pushed away by different queries, regardless of the semantic relationships.
